chunks: Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Fadhl narrated from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Abu al-Subbah al-Kinanī, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

He was asked about i'tikaf (spiritual retreat) in Ramadan during the last ten days. He said, 'Indeed, Ali (peace be upon him) used to say, 'I do not consider i'tikaf except in the Sacred Mosque (Al-Masjid al-Haram), or in the Messenger's Mosque (Al-Masjid al-Nabawi), or in a congregational mosque (Masjid Jami').''

Al-Sheikh (may Allah have mercy on him) said: 'And whoever breaks his fast without an excuse while he is in i'tikaf, or has sexual intercourse, the penalty that is obligatory upon one who does that deliberately without an excuse in the month of Ramadan becomes obligatory upon him.'
ai.seo_question: Where should i'tikaf be performed and what is the penalty for breaking fast during it?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes the juristic preference for i'tikaf to be confined to the three sanctified mosques (Mecca, Medina, and Jerusalem), a view attributed to Imam Ali (AS), while simultaneously clarifying that the penalties for breaking the fast or marital relations during retreat apply equally to the i'tikaf context. Shaykh al-Tusi’s commentary underscores the continuity of Ramadan's fasting laws within the spiritual enclosure, emphasizing that the sanctity of the location does not exempt one from the standard legal consequences of deliberate acts without valid excuse.
